title: The Oy Sound
kidRule: The 'oy' sound is usually spelled OI at the start or in the middle of a word and OY at the end. A few words, like royal, sneak OY into the middle.
hint: I hear the 'oy' sound. Is it in the middle of the word or right at the end? That tells you which team to pick.
reminder: The 'oy' sound is spelled O-I in the middle of a word and O-Y at the end.

check.question: Why does ENJOY end with OY and not OI?
check.correctAnswer: The 'oy' sound at the end of a word is spelled OY!
distractors: Because OI is only used in long words
Because Y always comes after the letter O

words.def: To like doing something a lot.
words.story: Rats enjoy being tickled! They make tiny happy squeaks that are too high for people to hear.
words.card: I jump for *joy* because I *enjoy* jelly on my pizza!

words.def: To stay away from something, or to keep it from happening.
words.sent: I walk on the grass to avoid the puddles.
words.story: Bats avoid bumping into things in the dark by making squeaks and listening for the echoes!
words.card: I *avoid* sharing my *avo*cado with the hungry seagull!

words.def: To bother someone and make them a little bit cross.
words.story: The buzz of a housefly, which can really annoy you, comes from its wings beating about 200 times every second!
words.card: It will *annoy* *an* alligator if you tickle his toes!

words.def: To break or wreck something completely.
words.sent: A big wave can destroy a sandcastle.
words.story: A big swarm of locusts can destroy as much food in one day as thousands of people would eat!
words.card: The b*est* way to *destroy* a sandcastle is one giant belly flop!

words.def: Something that can make people or animals very sick if they eat or touch it.
words.sent: The label warns that the berries contain poison.
words.story: Tiny poison dart frogs wear bright colors like yellow and blue to warn other animals: 'Do not eat me!'
words.card: The frog told her *son*, 'Our bright spots say we are full of *poison*, so nobody nibbles us!'

words.def: To feel or show great happiness.
words.sent: The whole town will rejoice when the team wins.
words.story: Rejoice and joy are word cousins. Both grew from the same old Latin word for being glad!
words.card: Penguins *rejoice* when the *ice* cream truck slides by!

words.def: To give someone a job and pay them for their work.
words.sent: The bakery will employ two new bakers this summer.
words.story: Some airports employ trained falcons and dogs to chase flocks of birds away from the runways, so planes can take off safely!
words.card: The cat's clever *ploy* was to *employ* a mouse as her alarm clock!

words.def: A smooth, greasy cream you rub on your skin to help it heal.
words.sent: Dad rubbed ointment on my scraped knee.
words.story: There is an old saying, 'a fly in the ointment'. It means one small problem in something that is otherwise good!
words.card: Three snow*men* asked for *ointment* to soothe their carrot noses!

words.def: A big rock that travels around the sun in space.
words.sent: An asteroid zoomed past the Earth last night.
words.story: The word asteroid means 'star-like', because through early telescopes these space rocks looked like tiny points of light!
words.card: An *aster* flower rode an *asteroid* all the way to Mars!

words.def: A thick, soft cloth with fuzzy raised stripes.
words.sent: My corduroy pants make a swishing sound when I walk.
words.story: The fuzzy raised stripes on corduroy have their own name: they are called wales!
words.card: *Roy* the snail wears *corduroy* pants, which is odd, because snails have no legs!
